almanac.notice.litelights_too_old: Almanac: far terrain's seasonal snow is off. LiteLights %s is older than %s, the first that works with this Almanac. Update LiteLights to turn it back on.
almanac.notice.litelights_climate: Almanac: LiteLights %s asks for seasonal biome copies, which this Almanac no longer has, so its weather looks go by each biome's own climate (rain and snow still follow the season). LiteLights %s or later works with this Almanac.
almanac.refused.no_almanac: %s needs Almanac %s in your game too, for its seasons. Install Almanac %s (Fabric) and join again.
almanac.refused.older_almanac: %s runs Almanac %s, and your Almanac %s is older than that and doesn't work with it. Install Almanac %s and join again.
almanac.refused.newer_almanac: %s runs Almanac %s, and your Almanac %s is newer than that and doesn't work with it. Install Almanac %s and join again.
almanac.settings.denied: Only operators can change the server settings.
almanac.settings.unreadable: The server couldn't read those settings, so nothing changed.
almanac.title: Almanac
almanac.look.tooltip: Switch this screen between the House look and a Minecraft-style look. Nothing else changes.
almanac.footer.mode.dark: Dark mode. Click to switch to light mode.
almanac.footer.mode.light: Light mode. Click to switch to dark mode.
almanac.description.empty: Point at a setting to see what it does.
almanac.reset.tooltip: Put this back to its default
almanac.note.server_read_only: These are the settings of the server you're playing on, as it last sent them. Only operators can change them, so ask one if you'd like something changed. Your own settings are on the "On this computer" page.
almanac.note.server_without_mod: This server doesn't have Almanac, so there are no server settings to show.
almanac.note.server_editable: These are the settings of the server you're playing on, as it last sent them. You may change them: when you press Done they go to the server, which checks them, saves them in its own config/almanac-server.json and sends them to every player. The file on this computer isn't touched.
almanac.note.server_singleplayer: These are this world's settings, from config/almanac-server.json on this computer. They apply when you press Done, and the next singleplayer world starts with them too.
almanac.note.server_local_file: No world is open, so these are the settings in config/almanac-server.json on this computer: the ones your next singleplayer world starts with. A server you join keeps its own.
almanac.note.climates: Every biome counts as temperate, cold or hot (the climate/temperate, climate/cold and climate/hot biome tags, then the common biome tags, then its temperature and rain), and the seasons move each climate's temperature through the year. Biomes in the no_seasonal_snow tag, jungles among them, never get the season's snow.
almanac.note.shares: Each storm brings rain or snow to a climate when the climate's share this sub-season is above the storm's own draw, so a bigger share gets everything a smaller one does. The rest pass over dry. Sub-seasons a climate is always dry in, such as summer in hot biomes, aren't listed. With regional weather off the shares are of vanilla's rain events instead.
almanac.note.weather_command: With regional weather, /weather rain or thunder places a still storm with a radius of 1,200 blocks over whoever runs it, for vanilla's times unless they give one, and /weather clear keeps the sky clear for 2,500 blocks around them. /almanac weather everywhere clear, rain or thunder changes the whole world either way.
almanac.note.this_computer: These are yours alone, kept in config/almanac-client.json on this computer, and you can change them on any server.
almanac.note.look: The buttons at the foot of the screen switch between Almanac's look and Minecraft's, and in Almanac's choose the accent colour and light or dark. They are kept with this computer's settings.
almanac.note.commands: /season shows the date. Operators have /season set, pause, resume and length; /almanac config lists, shows and changes every server setting by name, and /almanac config reload reads the file again after a hand edit; /almanac snow shows the snow; /almanac weather status, storms and forecast show the weather around you, and /almanac weather everywhere changes it for the whole world.
almanac.note.snow_clocks: Snow builds and melts a layer at a time on two clocks, and still water freezes over on a third. With regional weather the snow follows the storms: each patch of land has the snow of the storms that passed over it, and land that loads later is caught up from them, so it matches the land around it.
almanac.note.far_terrain: Distant Horizons and Voxy draw far land as it was when they last saw it. With a LiteLights version that supports it, that land shows the season's snow instead, from a coarse map of the biomes the server sends to every player.
almanac.note.palette: Seasonal colours come from assets/almanac/palette.json, which resource packs can replace.
almanac.note.permissions: The Seasons, Climate, Snow and ice and Weather pages are the server's settings. Connected to a server, they show the server's own values; operators (permission level 2 and up) can change them here, and the server checks the permission and every value itself, saves its config/almanac-server.json and sends the settings to everyone. Other players see them locked. In singleplayer, and on the title screen, they are this computer's config/almanac-server.json, which singleplayer worlds use. The "On this computer" page is yours alone and lives in config/almanac-client.json.
almanac.note.live_changes: Everything applies as soon as you press Done: the calendar, regional weather and the time under rain, the shares of storms, the snow line and the winter and summer temperatures, the snow clocks and the deepest snow, melting, catching up and far terrain. A new time under rain counts for the storms that form from the next weather day on; the storms already about, and the snow they left, stay as they were.
almanac.note.keys: Open this screen from Mod Menu, or bind a key under Options, Controls, Key Binds, Almanac. The key is unbound to start with.
almanac.note.players_need_almanac: From Almanac 0.2.0 every player needs the mod, of the same version as the server's: a server refuses a player without it, and so does a single-player world opened to LAN, with a message saying which Almanac to install. The console can change every setting with /almanac config.
almanac.note.credits: Almanac is new code under the MIT licence. Idea by Fabric Seasons (lucaargolo): biome edits in memory, tracking weather-placed snow. Idea by Serene Seasons (Glitchfiend): sub-seasons and rain timing. Idea by Immersive Snow Reloaded (Straywave and contributors): snow recalculation on chunk load. Idea by Create: Sky: regional weather with travelling storms, nothing falling above a storm's cloud top, a local /weather. Idea by Climate: Clouds, Storms, Technology: regional, moving weather. Idea by ProtoManly's Weather: regional, moving weather; storms worked out alike on the server and every client, from forming to fading; snow caught up from the storms that passed. Idea by Simple Clouds: clouds grouped where the weather is. No code, data or wording is copied from any of them.
almanac.setting.days_per_season.descript: How many in-game days each season lasts. Each season has an early, mid and late part, so the default 24 gives 8 days to each. The current sub-season and how far into it are kept when this changes. Drag the slider or type an exact number from 3 to 1200 in the box.
almanac.setting.start_sub_season.descrip: The sub-season a world's first day falls in. Changing it doesn't move a world that has already started; use /season set for that.
almanac.setting.paused.description: Stop the calendar. The days still pass, but the season stays where it is until this is switched off.
almanac.setting.announce_sub_seasons.des: Show "Mid Winter has begun" and the like above the hotbar when a sub-season begins.
almanac.setting.regional_weather.descrip: Storms that form, move across the land and pass, so it rains or snows in one place and not in another, and the snow lies where the storms went. Off, one weather for the whole world, as before Almanac 0.4.0.
almanac.setting.time_under_rain.descript: With regional weather, the share of the time every place is under a storm's rain or snow, the same in every season; vanilla rains about 16% of the time. Storms are 1.4 times as wide as Almanac 1.0.0's, and their number is worked out to give this share. A change counts for the storms that form from the next weather day on; the storms already about, and the weather and snow before, stay as they were.
almanac.setting.weather_command_everywhe: With regional weather, /weather rain or thunder places a storm over whoever runs it and /weather clear clears the sky around them. On, it changes the weather everywhere instead, as in vanilla; a world-wide clear stops the snow everywhere too. /almanac weather everywhere does that either way.
almanac.setting.snow_line_above_sea: Snow line in cold biomes' early and late summer
almanac.setting.snow_line_above_sea.desc: In early and late summer, cold biomes get rain below this many blocks above sea level and snow above it.
almanac.setting.winter_temperature.descr: The temperature given to warmer biomes when winter brings them snow. Vanilla snows below 0.15.
almanac.setting.summer_temperature.descr: The temperature given to cold biomes when summer brings them rain. Higher values raise the height at which rain turns to snow.
almanac.setting.snowfall_ticks.descripti: How long one layer of snow takes to build while it snows, in ticks. Two layers take twice as long. Loaded land, land that loads and far terrain all build at this pace.
almanac.setting.thaw_ticks.description: How long one layer of snow takes to melt while it is warm, in ticks, and how long frozen water takes to thaw. The top layer goes first.
almanac.setting.ice_ticks.description: How long still water takes to freeze over while it is cold, in ticks: the shore first, the middle last. 0 uses the snowfall clock.
almanac.setting.max_snow_layers.descript: How many layers deep the season's snow may build. Each further layer starts once the one under it is 90% down. A world an older Almanac let build deeper, with the snow height game rule, keeps that depth.
almanac.setting.native_snow_melts_in_sum: Snow that came with a snowy biome melts when summer makes it warm there, and comes back in fall. Only single layers on natural ground melt; snow players place, snow blocks and native ice never do.
almanac.setting.snow_catch_up: Bring loading chunks up to date
almanac.setting.snow_catch_up.descriptio: Chunks that load behind the season (new, or unloaded while it changed) get the season's snow and ice, or lose them, the moment they load. Part way through a snowfall or a thaw they get the share of each layer that loaded land has, on the same columns. Off, loaded land's own pace brings them up to date instead.
almanac.setting.catch_up_chunks_per_tick: Chunks brought up to date per tick
At most this many loading chunks are brought up to date each tick; the rest wait for the next tick.
almanac.setting.snow_columns_per_tick.de: How many columns of loaded chunks are brought to the season's snow and ice each tick; columns with nothing to change count as a sixteenth. All of loaded land's snow work comes from this. Higher keeps up faster and costs more.
almanac.setting.far_climate_map.descript: Sends players who have Almanac a coarse map of the biomes around them, worked out from the world generator without loading any chunks, so far terrain can show the season's snow. Off, their clients drop the map and far terrain stays as it was drawn.
almanac.setting.far_climate_radius.descr: How far the climate map reaches around each player. Match it to the far terrain's render distance; further costs more sampling on the server and more data for each player.
almanac.setting.far_climate_cell_size.de: The map has one biome per cell. Smaller cells follow biome borders more closely; each halving costs four times the sampling and about three times the data.
almanac.setting.far_climate_bytes_per_ti: At most this much of the climate map goes to each player every tick, nearest first, so joining or travelling never floods a connection.
almanac.setting.colour_blending.descript: Grass and leaves change a little every day. Off, they change once per sub-season.
almanac.setting.redraw_sections_per_tick: After a colour change, the loaded sections with grass or leaves are redrawn this many per tick, nearest first. Lower is smoother on slower computers; higher finishes sooner.
